scores.hardest: Seating a vesicular, irregular cinder so its pocket walls do not show: an air pocket shows every milled wall, a backfilled one draws air out of the vesicles.
scores.failure: Bubble trains rising out of the cinder's vesicles into the backfill during cure and again at the 70 C anneal, plus a silvered air film along the pocket walls.
scores.fix: Split the pocket across the bond line: mill a conformal half-pocket (from a scan, +0.4 mm) in each of the two clear blanks, sawn face down on a flat floor. Dry the cinder 24 h at 105 C, vacuum-impregnate with dilute shellac or a thin stabilizing resin so the vesicles are closed. Leave it in a dry air pocket and put the 3 mm Ember lamina on both large faces so the walls are seen only through tint; cement on the flats with a 0.3 mm square step at the pocket rim as a capillary stop.

scores.hardest: Getting a brittle sulfur cluster through bonding and a 70 C anneal: sulfur cracks on thermal ramp and may retard the cement's cure where it touches.
scores.failure: Crystals fracturing or clouding in the anneal ramp, and soft/tacky cement wherever monomer reached the sulfur.
scores.fix: Never let cement near it: dry air pocket, cluster fixed to its basalt chip and the chip pinned to the floor with a dot of epoxy, cement on flats only with a capillary-stop step at the rim and a 0.8 mm vent flushed 20 min then plugged. Ramp the anneal at 5 C/h max, hold 65 C. Drop the 'Dallol' name unless the material is Dallol; Sicilian legacy specimens make each piece unique, so this is a one-off, not an edition.

scores.hardest: Packing a 2 mm sand bed so it is full, level and does not shift, with no cement reaching the sand.
scores.failure: A wet-look dark band where cement wicks into the sand at the rim, or a sand bed that settles and leaves an air crescent.
scores.fix: Full-face pocket 2.00 mm deep leaving a 4 mm clear rim, sand washed, sieved 0.2-0.5 mm, oven-dried 120 C, screeded 0.1 mm proud and pressed flat with the lid. Cement only on the 4 mm rim, thickened, with a 1 x 0.5 mm moat between rim and sand to catch squeeze-out. The sand hides the pocket floor and its edge reads as a stratum, so the walls are a non-issue.

scores.hardest: Keeping a wood slice dimensionally still inside acrylic for decades.
scores.failure: Seasonal swelling breaking the bond or crazing the pocket rim, and tannin brown bleeding into any cement it touches.
scores.fix: Kiln-dry to 6 % MC, vacuum-stabilize with a heat-cured methacrylate resin (Cactus Juice type) and cure fully, seal with two coats of dewaxed shellac. Slice 4-5 mm, set in an air pocket 0.3 mm oversize all round so it can move; cement on flats with a rim step, never backfill. Ember/Poison strata over both faces hide the walls.

scores.hardest: Getting thin, hollow seed heads dry enough that the anneal raises no mist and no bubbles.
scores.failure: Moisture mist and a silvered halo around the stems after the anneal; over years bleaching from gold to grey and, if any moisture remains, mould spotting.
scores.fix: Freeze 72 h at -20 C (pests), dry in silica gel 2 weeks, seal with dilute shellac, store desiccated until bonding. Shallow air pocket 1.5 mm, floor bead-blasted to a uniform frost so it reads as a herbarium sheet and the tool marks disappear into it. Cement on flats only, rim step, anneal at 65 C. UV-absorbing clear grade for the cover sheet.

scores.hardest: A 160 mm laminated ball: about 160 h of anneal, many bond lines to keep bubble-free, and a large iron slice at the centre with a CTE about six times lower than the acrylic.
scores.failure: Rust blooming on the etched face within a few years (chloride in the iron) where it cannot be serviced; cold-weather cracks at the slice edges; a battery sealed in the same body is a venting hazard.
scores.fix: Chloride-reduce the slice (alkaline wash), dry, lacquer, and put it in a dry air pocket with 0.5 mm clearance all round and a hidden molecular-sieve cartridge, nitrogen-flushed via a vent then plugged. No battery or LED inside the same block; put any light in a separate base. Build the ball from two thick cast blocks rather than many laminae, one equatorial bond line.

scores.hardest: Hiding the air gap round a rounded pebble when seen through a clear top.
scores.failure: A silver crescent where the round pebble does not meet a milled pocket, visible through the top face.
scores.fix: Chert is dense and inert, so backfill is safe: set the pebble on a 0.5 mm acrylic pin, fill the pocket open in 2 mm lifts of degassed ACRIFIX 2R with a sprue to feed shrinkage, cure each lift 6 h, face-mill flat, then bond the Fog lid on flats. Or simpler: conformal split-pocket in both halves with the Fog strata hiding the walls.

scores.hardest: Twelve bond lines each carrying shallow lens voids that must stay cement-free: a feathered lens rim is a capillary wedge that sucks cement straight in.
scores.failure: Cement fingering into the lens rims (a frosted ring or a flooded lens) on a few of the twelve joints, so one bad joint scraps the whole weight; Newton's-ring halos where a cement-free margin is left.
scores.fix: Give every lens a 0.3 mm square step at its rim (a capillary stop) instead of a feathered edge; finish the dishes with a polished single-crystal diamond ball-nose at 0.01-0.02 mm stepover. Pre-dry and anneal the sheets 80 C, bond within 24 h. Better: drop cement here and solvent-assisted press bond (ethanol, 70-80 C, 1-2 MPa, flats lapped) or cut to 6 layers. Expect 1 good in 3 at 12 layers.

scores.hardest: Thousands of matched sub-millimetre hemispheres on three bond lines, aligned to 0.05 mm across a wall panel, each kept dry of cement.
scores.failure: Hundreds of half-flooded or mismatched voids (a ledge at every equator), and later crazing starting at void rims from edge-light heat cycling.
scores.fix: Use single-sided dimples on one face against a flat cover (no matching needed; still silver by TIR), density gradient by count not size, one or two bond lines, and a heated press bond (solvent-assisted, 70-90 C) rather than flowing cement. Keep the LED strip on a metal bar with an air gap to the edge.

scores.hardest: A void-free 160 mm-diameter equatorial bond with no cement creeping into the 40 mm sphere.
scores.failure: A faint equatorial plane or a bubble ring in the cement film; a cement tear at the rim of the sphere if the bead is overfed.
scores.fix: Turn each hemispherical pocket on the lathe with a diamond tool on oversize square cast blocks (axisymmetric, so optical straight off the tool), anneal, then bond face-to-face with degassed ACRIFIX 2R as an annular bead at mid-radius, pressed in a fixture; the sharp 90 deg rim of the hemisphere is a natural capillary stop. Drill a 1 mm vent, flush 20 min, plug with rod and cement. Wait 24 h, anneal 70 C, then turn the ball to 160 mm round the void. Keep it free of electronics.

scores.hardest: Registering two half-round grooves along a long closed contour so the channel is round, not stepped.
scores.failure: A visible ledge or flat along the line where the halves miss, and spots where cement wicked into the channel.
scores.fix: Mill the full D-section in one face only (1.5 mm deep, 3 mm wide, ball-nose, polished PCD, fine finishing pass) against a flat cover: no registration error, still silver by TIR. Rim step as capillary stop, cement on flats, one vent to the edge flushed and plugged. LED bar off the edge with an air gap.

scores.hardest: A modulated spiral channel at record-weight scale, cement kept out over its whole length.
scores.failure: Local floods where cement creeps into the channel; and under 29 % Smoke the silver line goes dull, so the waveform barely reads.
scores.fix: One-sided D-channel, polished cutter, rim step, cement on flats, single vent. Put the Smoke lamina under the channel (as a background) rather than over it, or use Ice on top, so the TIR line reads against dark.

scores.hardest: Vertical strings of spheres in a floor-lamp column mean either hundreds of bond lines or one long lengthwise seam, both in a structural part.
scores.failure: Voids acting as crack starters in a load-bearing column, and a long visible seam; a lamp body in HB acrylic is not an enclosure.
scores.fix: Split the column lengthwise into two thick halves, hemispheres on the seam only, solvent-assisted press bond; keep voids well clear of the light and any fastener; driver and mains in a metal base, acrylic decorative only. Or move the idea to a non-structural panel.

scores.hardest: Keeping the tape's polyurethane binder and lubricants away from any monomer.
scores.failure: Binder bleed or a brown halo where cement or its vapour reached the coil; oxide shedding into the pocket over time.
scores.fix: Dry air pocket exactly tape width + 0.3 mm deep, coil held by a turned clear hub, cement on flats with a rim step and a vent flushed 20 min before plugging. The Smoke lamina over the pocket hides the milled walls; bead-blast the floor. Use new-stock modern tape, never acetate base.

scores.hardest: Cutting the nickel stamper cleanly without burring or bending the groove field.
scores.failure: Cement or monomer vapour filming the grooves and killing the diffraction, or a raised burr tenting the cover.
scores.fix: Wire-EDM or fine waterjet the shard, deburr, ultrasonic clean. Pocket 0.2 mm deeper than the shard, grooves up and not touching the cover; cement on flats with a rim step. A shallow pocket viewed face-on shows almost no wall.

scores.hardest: Holding a 6 mm cantilever and a sub-millimetre diamond still and readable in a plinth corner.
scores.failure: The part shifts or tilts in its pocket, or a dust speck sealed in beside it reads larger than the stylus under the lens.
scores.fix: Bare cantilever and tip only (no plastic body), glued to a turned clear acrylic pin; bore the pocket on the viewing axis so the walls are seen edge-on and vanish; polished convex dome over it (R about 15 mm) as a 2x magnifier. Bond in a clean hood, cement on flats, vent and plug.

scores.hardest: Flattening odd offcuts of different tints and thicknesses to one thickness and bonding many laminae without bubbles.
scores.failure: A bubble or dry patch in one of eight bond lines, or crazing on an unannealed offcut edge.
scores.fix: Fly-cut every disc to 3.00 +/- 0.05 mm, pre-anneal 80 C, bond in one stack with degassed ACRIFIX 2R under even platen pressure, wait 24 h, anneal 70 C at about 1 h/mm, then turn and polish the OD. Same polymer throughout, so nothing to outgas or fade.

scores.hardest: Bonding polyester film: cement does not adhere well to PET, and the print may smear in monomer.
scores.failure: Silvered delaminations across the film within a year or two, and an ink haze; PET at n about 1.65 also shows as a full-face ghost.
scores.fix: Do not bond the film. Float it unbonded in a 0.4 mm recess cut by a fly-cutter, with cement only on a 10 mm perimeter frame, vented and plugged; or drop the film and laser-engrave the drawing on the inner face of the back sheet inside the same sealed air recess, where the lines read as frost.

notes: The editions that stay inside what a laminating shop already does well (same-polymer strata, inert flat or dense objects in dry pockets, one big turned void) will ship; the many-bond-line void fields and the organics will eat yield. For bubbles, the enemy is the feathered edge: a lens or dish that meets the flat at a knife edge is a capillary wedge and pulls cement in, so every void gets a 0.3 mm square step at its rim as a capillary stop, cement applied as a degassed bead on the flats sized so the squeeze-out front pins at that step, a drilled vent flushed 20 min then plugged, sheets pre-dried and annealed at 80 C before bonding, 24 h wait, anneal at 70 C with a slow ramp (air at +18 % is no threat to small voids). Where there are many voids or bond lines, drop flowing cement for a solvent-assisted press bond (ethanol, 70-90 C, 1-2 MPa, lapped flats). Axisymmetric voids should be diamond-turned on the lathe, not milled, so their walls are optical off the tool. Pocket walls cannot be hidden by polish in an air pocket; hide them by viewing them edge-on (pockets bored on the view axis), by putting a tinted lamina over them, by bead-blasting the floor as a deliberate ground, or, only for inert dense objects, by backfilling with index-matched ACRIFIX in 2 mm open lifts with a sprue, then face-milling and bonding the lid.
